html:
The Yueban, or Örpün, were a nomadic people of Zhetysu, the Seven Rivers country of southeastern Kazakhstan, from about the 2nd to the 5th century. Chinese historians saw them as remnants of the Northern Xiongnu and called them the "weak Xiongnu".

When the Northern Xiongnu were broken by Han China and its allies around 90, most of them fled west out of Chinese knowledge. The Yueban stayed closer to China and kept in contact with it. In the 400s they sent envoys to the Northern Wei dynasty of north China, seeking an ally against the Rouran, the new masters of Mongolia. Their neighbours to the east included the Southern Xiongnu, who had gone over to China.

In the 480s the Yueban split into four tribes. One of them later mixed with the Türks and became the Shatuo, who went on to found dynasties in northern China in the 900s.
